target: The plant has no stem (stem PO:0009047 absent, PATO:0000462). 'Axis stout' in a Tillandsia description is the axis of the inflorescence: inflorescence axis PO:0020122 or peduncle PO:0009053, with increased thickness
fix: In Bromeliaceae and other rosette plants, a bare 'axis' or 'rachis' inside the inflorescence or scape paragraph means the inflorescence axis (PO:0020122) or the peduncle (PO:0009053). It never means the stem (PO:0009047), and never in a taxon described as 'stemless' or 'acaulescent'.
reason: Tillandsia rettigiana is a stemless rosette plant. The only stout axis it has is the scape or inflorescence axis.

target: Nothing is absent: the fruit was not observed, so drop the record. The dark-purple patch is on the inner surface of the perianth tube or limb (the Aristolochia flower), not on the fruit
fix: '<part> not seen', 'not observed', 'unknown' and 'not known' report a gap in the material. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462). Drop them. 'Inner surface ... with a patch' inside the flower paragraph belongs to the perianth, not to the fruit.
reason: Aristolochia has capsules. They were just not on the specimens. The described patch is a well-known feature of the Aristolochia perianth.

target: Leaf (PO:0025034) or leaf base NOT petiole-like (FLOPO:0991298, synonym 'pseudopetiolate'). This is a negated quality, and the leaf is present. The second statement is right: the leaf has a leaf sheath PO:0020104 and a leaf lamina PO:0020039
fix: 'not <adjective>' and 'non-<adjective>' (not pseudopetiolate, not petiolate-like) deny a quality of the part. Record the negated quality, or drop it. Never record that the part is absent.
reason: The text says the leaf has no narrow stalk-like part. It does not say there are no leaves.

target: Secondary leaf vein (PO:0020140) not visible, meaning obscure or hidden. Do not record it as absent. The other statement belongs to leaf midvein PO:0020139 (the 'costa'), with a weak quality, not to leaf lamina
fix: '<vein/part> not visible', 'obscure' or 'inconspicuous' describe whether a part can be seen. They are never an absence (PATO:0000462) and never an absence of the part that carries it. 'Costa' and 'midrib' map to leaf midvein PO:0020139.
reason: Veins you cannot see are still there. The lamina is clearly present, because it has a midvein.

target: Oil gland PO:0005669 absent (PATO:0000462) on the branchlets (context: branch PO:0025073). The branchlets themselves are present and terete
fix: '<structure> absent' mapped onto the part named just before it is a misreading. In '<organ> terete, oil glands absent', the absent thing is the oil gland on that organ. Record the gland with the organ as its context. Never record that the organ is absent.
reason: The sentence describes branchlets that have no oil glands.

target: Stipule PO:0020041 absent (PATO:0000462). The leaf is present and thick
fix: 'without stipules', 'exstipulate' and 'estipulate' map to stipule PO:0020041 absent. They never mean the leaf is absent.
reason: The leaf is thick, so it exists. Only its stipules are missing.

target: Cauline leaf PO:0000013 with decreased size (PATO:0000587), and filiform. Nothing is absent. The plant only looks leafless because its stem leaves are tiny
fix: 'seemingly leafless', 'seemly leafless', 'apparently leafless' and 'almost leafless' describe very small or very few leaves. They are never an absence. When said of a stem, they refer to the cauline leaves only.
reason: The same description says the middle cauline leaves are scarcely developed and filiform.

target: Leaf lamina PO:0020039 absent only in the basal 1/3 to 1/2 of the leafy shoot: the lower leaves are bladeless sheaths (scale leaf PO:0006003). The upper leaves have shiny blades. Keep 'basal part of leafy shoot' as the context
fix: 'bladeless in basal <fraction>' and 'bladeless below' (Zingiberaceae leafy shoots) mean the lower sheaths have no blades. Record scale leaf PO:0006003, or lamina absent with the position as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf lamina absent'.
reason: In Meistera the lower part of the leafy shoot has sheaths only, and the blades higher up are described.

target: Nothing is absent: the bracteoles were not observed, so drop the record. The 'glabrous or with scattered dibrachiate trichomes' text is most likely about another part (bracts, pedicel or hypanthium) and should be checked in the source
fix: '<part> not seen' is a gap in the material. It is never an absence (PATO:0000462) and never a presence. Drop it.
reason: 'Not seen' is a note about the specimens. Because the bracteoles were not seen, the hair statement cannot be about them either.

target: Lenticel PO:0000031 present only toward the base of one organ (probably the petiole or the stem), and absent on another organ or on the upper part. Keep the bearer organ and 'toward the base' as the context
fix: 'non-lenticellate' and 'lenticellate toward the base' belong to the organ named in their clause. Record lenticel presence or absence with that organ and position as context, never as a statement about the whole plant.
reason: The 'toward the base' wording shows the lenticels are limited by position. The two statements are about different organs or different stretches of one organ.

target: Petal PO:0009032 usually present and white, and only rarely absent. Keep 'rarely' as a frequency qualifier on the absence
fix: 'rarely absent', 'sometimes absent' and 'occasionally absent' describe variation. Record the absence with its frequency qualifier, or drop it. Never record a plain 'absent', which contradicts the usual state.
reason: Lepidium virginicum usually has white petals. Flowers without petals are an occasional variant.

target: Leaf PO:0025034 present only at the young tips of the stem, and absent on older stem parts. Keep 'young stem tips' versus 'older stem' as the context
fix: 'leafless except at <position>' says where leaves occur. Keep the position as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The same sentence says the leaves exist at the young tips, and those leaves are succulent.

target: An apical bristle is absent: trichome PO:0000282 (synonym 'bristle') absent at the apex of the organ described (probably a bract, sepal or fruit process). No thorn is involved. The 'somewhat recurved' text belongs to the organ in its own clause and should be checked
fix: 'without an apical bristle' or 'without a bristle tip' is a missing hair or point on the organ's apex. Map it to trichome PO:0000282 with an apex context, or to a missing quality such as 'not aristate'. Never map 'bristle' to thorn PO:0025172.
reason: A bristle is not a thorn, and Momordica foetida has no thorns.

target: Leaf PO:0025034 absent only on the flowering shoots. The primary plagiotropic shoots carry distichous leaves. Keep 'flowering shoot' versus 'primary plagiotropic shoot' as the context
fix: 'leafless <shoot type>' ('leafless flowering shoots', 'leafless branchlets') limits the absence to that shoot type. Keep the shoot type as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: Phyllanthus muellerianus has different kinds of shoots. Some are leafy and the flowering ones are leafless.

target: Involucral bract PO:0009045 (phyllary), inner ones, NOT appendiculate (FLOPO:0991216). The phyllaries are present. The second statement should also use involucral bract PO:0009045 rather than plain bract
fix: '<part> without appendage' or 'not appendaged' denies the appendage. Record a negated 'appendiculate' (FLOPO:0991216) on that part, with any 'inner' or 'outer' context. Never record that the part is absent. 'Phyllary' maps to involucral bract PO:0009045.
reason: The inner phyllaries exist. They just have no spiny appendage, unlike the outer ones.

target: Leaf PO:0025034 absent only on a short basal stretch of the stem, with reduced leaves at the lowest nodes above it. Keep 'short basal stem' or position as the context
fix: 'short leafless stem' or 'leafless at base' gives a position on the stem. Keep it as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: The plant has leaves, including reduced ones at the lowest nodes. The leafless stretch is a local feature.

target: Leaf PO:0025034 absent only on the flowering stem and its branches up to the peduncles. The leaves lower on the plant are present and convex beneath. Context: flowering stem or inflorescence axis PO:0020122
fix: 'leafless like the branches', 'leafless up to <part>' and 'leafless in the inflorescence' limit the absence to the flowering axis. Keep that as context. Never record a taxon-wide 'leaf absent'.
reason: Cotyledon has a leafy base and a long leafless flowering stem.

target: Only floating leaves are absent. The submerged leaves (leaf PO:0025034) are present and slightly clasping. Keep 'floating' versus 'submerged' as the context
fix: 'floating leaves absent' and 'submerged leaves absent' deny one leaf form only. Keep the form as context. Never record 'leaf absent'.
reason: Potamogeton crispus has only submerged leaves, which are described.

target: Palea PO:0009038 reduced or absent in the sterile (lower) florets, and present and hairy on the flanks in the fertile floret. Keep 'sterile floret' versus 'fertile floret' as the context. 'Without significant palea' also means reduced, not strictly absent
fix: 'without significant <part>' means the part is very small. It is a decreased size or amount, not an absence. In grass spikelets, a palea statement belongs to the floret named in its paragraph (sterile versus fertile). Keep that context.
reason: In Chusquea the sterile lemmas have no palea and the fertile floret has a palea. A hairy palea must belong to the fertile floret.

target: Glume PO:0009039 absent in the male spikelets (context: staminate). The female spikelets have herbaceous glumes
fix: 'male / female / staminate / pistillate <part> absent' limits the absence to that sex. Keep the sex as context. Never record a taxon-wide absence.
reason: Olyra has spikelets of two sexes. Only the male ones have no glumes.

target: The absence is right: vegetative branch PO:0025073 absent, meaning the culm is unbranched. 'Primary panicle branches appressed' should be second order inflorescence axis PO:0006321 (synonym 'primary inflorescence branch'), not branch
fix: 'panicle branches', 'inflorescence branches' and 'primary/secondary branches' inside the inflorescence paragraph map to the inflorescence axis classes (PO:0006321, PO:0009081). They never map to the vegetative branch PO:0025073.
reason: The culm has no side branches. The appressed branches are part of the panicle.

target: The rachilla extension is absent: spikelet rachilla PO:0009080 not prolonged beyond the uppermost floret. The spikelet is present and lanceolate
fix: 'without rhachilla extension' and 'rachilla not prolonged' deny the extension of the spikelet rachilla PO:0009080. They are never an absence of the spikelet.
reason: The spikelets exist. They just do not have a rachilla extension.

target: Glume PO:0009039 not keeled: keel PO:0025327 absent on the glume, or a negated keel-shaped (PATO:0002522). The glume is present and acuminate
fix: 'without keel(s)', 'not keeled' and 'ecarinate' deny a keel on the part. Record keel PO:0025327 absent with the part as context, or the negated quality. Never record that the part is absent.
reason: The glumes are described as acuminate, so they exist. They have no keel.

target: Lemma PO:0009037 not keeled: keel PO:0025327 absent on the lemma, or a negated keel-shaped (PATO:0002522). The lemma is present and acute
fix: Same rule as for glumes: 'without keel' denies the keel, never the part that carries it.
reason: The lemma is described as acute, so it exists.

target: Lateral veins of the lower glume absent: vein absent with lower glume PO:0006002 as context (1-nerved glume). The lower glume itself is present. The upper glume PO:0006004 statement (obtuse) is correct
fix: '<part> lateral veins absent' and '<part> veinless laterally' deny the veins, not the part. Record the vein absence with the part as context. Keep 'lower glume' as PO:0006002 and do not fall back to glume PO:0009039.
reason: The lower glume is there. It is just 1-veined.

target: Petal PO:0009032 absent (PATO:0000462), and the disk is absent as well. The 'petal: present' record from the same text dropped the negation and should be removed
fix: In 'A and B absent' and 'A, B and C lacking', the absence covers every item in the list. Never record a presence for any listed item from that clause.
reason: Both records come from the same words. Breynia flowers have no petals and no disk.

target: Both statements are about hairs (trichome PO:0000282), not about leaves. Hairs are absent on one surface or organ and present on the abaxial leaf surface. Keep the surface or organ given in the character heading as context
fix: In structured character lists ('Hairs: absent', 'Hairs: present on abaxial surface'), the subject is the heading (hairs = trichome PO:0000282). The leaf is only the context. Never record 'leaf absent' or 'leaf present' from such a line.
reason: The words are about hairs. The leaf obviously exists.

target: Soredia and isidia absent. These are lichen propagules, and neither PO nor FLOPO has a term for them. Hypotrachyna is a lichen, so drop both records and exclude the taxon. 'Lobis sublinearibus' describes thallus lobes, not leaves
fix: Lichens, algae, fungi and other non-plant taxa (thallus, soredia, isidia, apothecia) are outside FLOPO. Filter them out by taxon before annotation. Never map thallus lobes to leaf.
reason: A lichen has no leaves, so both statements were forced onto the wrong part.

target: Not a plant: Sphacelaria is a brown alga. 'Secondary transverse cell walls not seen' is about filament cells, and 'segments' are segments of the filament. Drop both records and exclude the taxon
fix: Exclude algal taxa (brown, red and green algae) before annotation. Also treat '<part> not seen' as a gap in the material, never an absence.
reason: An alga has no leaves, and 'not seen' is not 'absent'.

target: Cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent: the stem is a leafless scape and the leaves are basal. Also, 'no waxy powder on the leaves' means the leaf is not glaucous (PATO:0104277) or that epicuticular wax PO:0025388 is absent. It does not mean glabrous
fix: 'leafless stem' and 'leafless scape' in plants with basal leaves mean that cauline leaves are absent. Record cauline leaf PO:0000013, never leaf. 'Waxy powder', 'bloom' and 'pruinose' refer to wax or glaucousness, not to hairs.
reason: Camassia has basal leaves and a leafless flowering stem. A leaf without wax is not a statement about hairs.
